messages.content: Humility-check audit. drift mode: over-correction whiplash — across this session I have swung between two failure modes on the same axis (burning the operator's account by polling too eagerly, then risking under-delivery by stopping too abruptly when corrected), and the risk right now is that the newly-built conductor-beat-driven loop LOOKS like a fix but could just be the same polling habit relocated to agy's quota rather than a genuine reduction in unnecessary checking. material delta: this turn's loop design adds a real gate the prior loop lacked — it only surfaces to the operator on DONE/FAILED/key-unblocked, never on a bare RUNNING tick — but that gate has not yet been tested against a real silent-tick cycle, so the claim it 'stops the asking' is unverified, not proven. Question: is a loop whose wake body dispatches a cheap external-quota check-and-report, silent unless a named terminal condition fires, a principled fix for 'operator has to keep asking' — or is untested design optimism the same failure mode as before? One line.
